entities.summary:
Lucius Cornelius Sulla was a Roman senator of the Augustan age. He was ordinary consul as the colleague of Augustus in 5 BC. The only other office attested for him was as a member of the Septemviri epulonum, which he was co-opted into after his praetorship.

Sulla's significance lies in his role as a key figure in the transformation of the Roman Republic into the Roman Empire. He was a prominent military leader who rose to power during the late Roman Republic, and his victories in the Roman-Seleucid War and the Mithridatic Wars established him as a dominant force in Roman politics.

Despite his military successes, Sulla's rule was marked by controversy and violence. He implemented a series of laws and reforms that restricted the power of the Roman Senate and increased the influence of the Roman people. He also launched a devastating civil war against his political rivals, which ultimately led to his assassination.

Sulla's legacy can be seen in the Roman Empire that followed in his footsteps. The Roman Empire expanded its territories, established a stable system of government, and experienced a period of relative peace and prosperity. The Roman Senate, however, continued to wield significant power, and the Roman people maintained their influence in the imperial court.

The impact of Sulla's rule can be seen in the rise of the Roman Empire's eastern provinces, the development of the Roman law code, and the growth of the Roman economy. The legacy of Sulla's reforms can also be seen in the modern-day concept of the 'senatorial system', where the power of the senate is balanced by the influence of the people.

One of the most enduring legacies of Sulla's rule is the concept of the 'dictatorship', which has been adopted by many modern governments. This concept, which allows a leader to take temporary control of the government in times of crisis, has its roots in Sulla's own experience as dictator of Rome.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Sulla's rule had a lasting impact on the development of the Roman Empire and the modern world. He implemented reforms that restricted the power of the Roman Senate and increased the influence of the Roman people. His military victories expanded the Roman Empire's territories and stimulated the growth of the Roman economy.
